# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Taylor Alvarez
**Member ID:** W414846479
**Reference number:** POC-148BC2A38D-62382
**Date of denial notice:** August 16, 2026
**Service denied:** Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
**Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross (Commercial/ACA), State of California
**Governing policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery, effective 11/15/2025 — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/PDF-Joint-Surgery-2025-11-15.pdf

To: Anthem Blue Cross — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

Date: [Date I am sending this letter]

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 16, 2026 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve this surgery.

I am writing because the records already in my file appear to line up, point by point, with the plan's own published criteria under the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery. Below I have set out the plan's language and the matching documentation. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed for my hip.

## The plan's criteria and the records in my file

**1. Symptoms**

The policy states:

> "Moderate to severe hip pain (primarily in the groin) worsened by flexion activities (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) that interferes with activities of daily living and is not explained by another diagnosis"

My records document nine months of progressive pain in the hip that is not relieved by rest. They describe sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and that I cannot run or squat.

**2. Examination**

The policy states:

> "Positive impingement sign on clinical examination, defined as pain elicited with 90 degrees of flexion and internal rotation and adduction of the femur OR with extension and external rotation"

My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**3. Imaging**

The policy states:

> "Imaging studies (radiographs, MRI, or 3D computed tomography) show cam impingement evidenced by ONE or more of the following:"

and includes among those findings:

> "Femoral head-neck offset with an alpha angle greater than or equal to 55 degrees"

My MRI arthrogram of the hip dated July 7, 2026 documents cam-type femoroacetabular impingement with an alpha angle of 68 degrees. That is above the threshold the policy itself sets.

I would note that the excerpt above ends in a colon and introduces a list of findings that was not reproduced in the criteria I was given. If the plan relied on any other item from that list, I ask that it identify the specific criterion it applied.

**4. No advanced arthritis or severe cartilage damage**

The policy states:

> "No evidence of advanced osteoarthritis, defined as Tönnis grade ≥ 2, or joint space < 2 mm"

and

> "No evidence of severe (modified Outerbridge grade IV) chondral damage"

My imaging report documents that the joint space is preserved and that I am Tönnis grade 0. My records do not describe severe chondral damage. If the plan believes either of these exclusions applies to me, I ask that it point to the specific finding in my records that it relied on.

**5. Conservative management**

The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative management for a duration of at least 12 weeks*, including avoidance of hip stretching or any activity that elicits or aggravates symptoms"

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My file documents 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, from April 14, 2026 through July 21, 2026, with 18 visits completed. This is recorded in my physical therapy discharge note, which also documents my compliance. Alongside physical therapy, I took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on May 14, 2026 that gave only two weeks of partial relief. That is physical therapy plus more than one complementary treatment strategy, over a period longer than the 12 weeks the policy requires.

The policy also states:

> "*Less than the full duration of conservative management is permitted for an alpha angle greater than 65 degrees"

My alpha angle is 68 degrees, so even a shorter course would have satisfied this criterion. I completed more than the full duration.

**6. No improvement on reevaluation**

The policy states:

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My records describe nine months of *progressive* pain that was not relieved by rest, inadequate relief from NSAIDs, and only two weeks of partial relief from the injection. At the conclusion of 18 physical therapy visits, I still had sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting and could not run or squat.

**7. Causal association between the impingement and the damage**

The policy states:

> "Documentation of a likely causal association between the femoroacetabular impingement morphology and damage, e.g., a pistol-grip deformity with a tear of the acetabular labrum and articular cartilage damage in the anterosuperior quadrant"

My MRI arthrogram documents an anterosuperior labral tear together with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees — the impingement morphology and the labral damage in the same hip, in the same study.

**8. Imaging report submitted**

The policy states:

> "Imaging report. The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure."

My MRI arthrogram was obtained on July 7, 2026, well within 12 months of the request, and its findings correlate with my documented groin pain on flexion activities and my positive provocative testing.

## What I am asking the plan to do

The denial notice states only that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. It does not tell me which criterion I failed to meet. Based on the criteria above, the records in my file appear to address each requirement the plan has published.

I respectfully ask the plan to:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914, as requested by Dr. Marchetti; or
2. If the denial is upheld, identify in writing the specific criterion from the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Musculoskeletal — Joint Surgery that the plan found unmet, and the specific document or finding in my records that it relied on, along with the credentials of the reviewer who made the decision.

I also ask that my full prior authorization packet be reviewed, including my MRI arthrogram report of July 7, 2026 and my physical therapy discharge note. I am happy to supply anything further that would help, and I ask that my surgeon be given the opportunity to discuss my case with the reviewer.

Please note that some of the criteria excerpts available to me end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not able to review. To the extent the plan's decision rests on any criterion not reproduced above, I ask that it be identified so I can respond to it.

## Deadline and submission

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date, by **February 12, 2027**. I am submitting this letter before that date.

I am sending this appeal in writing to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. If you would like me to submit it in any other form, or if you need anything else from me to process it, please let me know and I will provide it promptly.

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Alvarez**

Reference number: POC-148BC2A38D-62382
